subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public prime, phase, or stagger controls for heartbeat and cron `every` schedules, and if so which persisted config/API/CLI contract should become canonical?
rationale: The remaining work changes public scheduling semantics and config/API/persistence surfaces, and repository policy makes config/default additions and compatibility behavior maintainer-owned product decisions.

options.title: Design narrow phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` phase or stagger contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, upgrade tests, and observability before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve fixed anchored `every` semantics and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat phases plus cron-expression staggering.

options.title: Adopt broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with migration and compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Design narrow phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` phase or stagger contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, upgrade tests, and observability before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the strongest current-history signal for cron stagger product boundaries and protocol/docs behavior.
